title: Chemical Fume Hood

references.label: Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories (BMBL)

purpose: Ventilates and exhausts airborne chemical vapors, fumes, and dust away from the operator during work with volatile or hazardous chemicals — a chemical engineering control, distinct from a biological safety cabinet, which is designed for biological aerosol containment rather than chemical vapor removal.
operatingPrinciple: A dedicated exhaust fan continuously draws room air in through the open sash and vents it (often through additional filtration/scrubbing, depending on the chemical) to the outside or a treatment system, creating an inward airflow that captures vapors generated at the work surface before they reach the operator's breathing zone.
basicOperation: Confirm adequate face velocity/airflow (often indicated by a flow monitor or alarm on the unit) before beginning work.
Work with the sash at the height marked/recommended by the manufacturer or facility policy — typically as low as practical while still allowing hand access.
Keep the work at least several inches back from the sash opening (not right at the face of the hood) to stay within the effective capture zone.
Avoid rapid arm movements or storing large equipment near the opening, both of which disrupt the inward airflow pattern.
Lower the sash fully when the hood is not actively in use.
importantSettings: Sash height (affects both face velocity and physical protection from splashes)
calibration: Periodic professional certification of face velocity and airflow performance per facility schedule.
maintenance: Do not use as general storage — clutter disrupts airflow and reduces the effective work area.
Report any airflow alarm, unusual noise, or loss of visible capture (e.g. via a tissue/smoke test) to facility maintenance.

commonErrors.problem: Chemical odor detected outside the hood
commonErrors.cause: Sash raised too high, work positioned too close to the opening, or airflow disrupted by clutter/rapid movement
commonErrors.fix: Lower the sash to the recommended height, work further back from the opening, and remove unnecessary items from inside the hood

commonErrors.problem: Confusing a fume hood with a biosafety cabinet for biological containment work
commonErrors.cause: A fume hood is not HEPA-filtered and does not protect against biological aerosols the way a certified BSC does
commonErrors.fix: Use a certified biological safety cabinet for biological aerosol-generating work; reserve the fume hood for chemical vapor work

safety: Never use a chemical fume hood as a substitute for a biological safety cabinet — it is not HEPA-filtered and does not contain biological aerosols the way a BSC does.
Keep the sash at the recommended working height at all times, not just during active manipulation.
Do not disable or override an airflow alarm.
